verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission successfully completed its 10-day journey.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "historic 10-day trip to the moon" (R2); "approximate 10-day mission around the Moon and back" (R4); "10-day mission to the moon and back" (R5); successful splashdown reported across sources
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm the mission lasted ~10 days and ended successfully with splashdown.

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. ET on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego... at 8:07 p.m. ET" (R2); "splashdown... at 8:07 p.m. EDT" (R4); "off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. ET" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Exact location, time, and date match across sources.

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission tested life-support systems around the Moon.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "check out all of (Orion's) environmental control, life support systems... before heading to the moon" (R1); "testing life‑support... systems in deep space" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm life-support testing during the mission in deep space, but not explicitly 'around the Moon'; broader testing context applies.

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission did not land on the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit. Instead... loop around it" (R1); "didn't land on the moon" (R3); "without landing" (R5); "won't touch down on the lunar surface" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated in multiple sources that no landing occurred.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission was the first crewed flight to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first piloted moonshot since... Apollo program 53 years ago" (R1); "first lunar voyage in more than a half-century" (R3); "first humans in over 50 years to venture to the Moon" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of being first crewed lunar mission since Apollo era.

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and... Jeremy Hansen" (R1); repeated exact crew list across sources
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names listed consistently in sources.

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission safely splashed down.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "perfect bullseye splashdown" (R2); "safely extracted" (R4); "safely back on Earth" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All sources report safe, successful splashdown.

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission were recovered by the U.S. Navy.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "U.S. Navy MH-60... Navy divers... USS John P. Murtha" (R2); "U.S. Navy helicopters... USS John P. Murtha" (R4); "U.S. Navy sailors... dive team" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit U.S. Navy involvement in recovery confirmed.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission was a test flight to fly around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "test flight... loop around [the moon]" (R1); "test flight for future moon missions... lunar flyby" (R3); "test mission to the moon... loop around the moon" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Described as test flight specifically to flyby/loop around Moon.

verifications.claim: The first landing of the Artemis program is planned for a later mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis IV will attempt to land... in 2028" (R3); "first moon landing... on Artemis 4, no earlier than 2028" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first landing on later Artemis mission (3 or 4).

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission traveled over 250,000 miles from Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission set a new record for the farthest humans have ever traveled.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "travel farther from Earth than anyone before them" (R1); "set the record for the farthest distance any human has traveled from Earth — 252,756 miles" (R2); "broke Apollo 13's distance record" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated as new record for farthest distance.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission validated the Orion spacecraft systems with crew
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "thoroughly test their Orion capsule... first with a crew" (R1); "confirm all the spacecraft’s systems operate as designed with crew aboard" (R8); "tested space hardware and life support systems" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Mission purpose was to validate/test Orion systems with crew.
